subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the intro call today. I pulled together a short recap of the pain points and what we heard, plus proposed next steps so we all stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level summary (what you told us):
- Primary problem: inference unit economics are putting pressure on product roadmap. Current spend is growing faster than revenue from the feature.
- Current stack: mixing hosted API (3rd-party model provider) and some in-house GPU hosts; no centralized KV/prefix caching.
- Numbers called out: ~150M tokens/month today, average cost ~ $2.6k/day (variable by model), wanting 50-70% reduction in per-token spend to keep feature economics viable.
- Latency SLO: p95 target ~ <300ms for primary inference requests (customer-facing).
- Openness to tradeoffs: team is open to quantization and slightly lower-quality model variants if unit economics improve materially.

Success criteria for a short PoC:
- Demonstrate 2x-3x cost reduction on the same workload (token-normalized)
- Maintain p95 latency <300ms for the majority of traffic (with bursting allowed)
- Minimal engineering changes on your side for a short trial (we can run transparent routing or sidecar in front of your stack)

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive (SE call) to share token-profile and sample requests - schedule with Dev (cc'd) - target next Tue/Wed.
2) We’ll send a short PoC outline + expected benchmarks and a lightweight data request (sample traffic, 1-2 days of traces). See attached: redwood-poc-outline.pdf.
3) Pricing & capacity note: I’ll include a baseline estimate based on the numbers you shared and 2 quantization/batching scenarios.

If that looks right, would you be open to a 45-min SE session next week? Dev can drive the benchmarking plan.

Thanks - talk soon.

-
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
redwood.ai
From: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morales <alex.morales@finbot.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Thanks Marissa - this is a great summary and matches our notes. A few clarifications and additional context from our side: 

Clarifications / current stack details:
- We run the majority of user-facing generation through a 3rd-party hosted LLM provider (commercial model) and batch lower-priority tasks on a small fleet of EC2 GPU instances (self-managed).
- Monthly volume: ~150M tokens (user prompts + assistant responses). Peak concurrency ~120 rps.
- Average per-token bill (combined): ~ $0.017/token (this is the blended rate across legacy discounts and burst pricing).

Pain / constraints:
- Finance is pushing for immediate unit-cost improvements - we need to get to a place where marginal cost per active user is < $0.50/month for our main use case.
- We cannot tolerate significant quality regressions for our high-value flows (onboarding conversations).

Openness to technical changes:
- We are open to quantization and smaller model variants on lower-priority flows. For customer-facing onboarding, we want to prioritize latency and quality; willing to test quantized/optimized variants behind a canary.
- We have some instrumentation but no centralized prefix/KV cache today - would welcome guidance on integration complexity.

Next steps from our side: we can share a small sample of traffic (anonymized) and a cost workbook; I attached finbot-token-costs.xlsx. SE deep-dive works for us - Alex and I are available Tue 2/24 10-12 PST or Wed 2/25 1-4 PST.

Sophie
Head of Product, FinBot
sophie.zhang@finbot.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@finbot.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Perfect - thanks for the detail and the worksheet, Sophie. Dev and I will take a look and propose a concrete test plan. Quick notes for the SE session: 

Agenda (45 min):
- 10m: Walk through sample traffic and token profile (FinBot)
- 15m: Redwood architecture options - batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization profiles we recommend for similar workloads
- 15m: Benchmark plan & PoC success metrics (cost normalized + latency targets)
- 5m: Next steps + timeline and data/credential asks

We’ll come prepared with two candidate approaches:
A) Minimal integration: routing subset of traffic through Redwood hosted (no infra changes) to measure real savings + fallbacks.
B) Deeper integration: lightweight sidecar + KV cache on your infra for maximum unit-cost reduction (requires a small engineering effort).

Dev - are you free Tue 2/24 10:30-11:15 PST to run the session? If not, we can do Wed 2/25 1:30-2:15 PST per Sophie’s windows.

Thanks - I’ll schedule the call once we confirm a time and will attach the PoC outline + basic SOW.

-
Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Internal - quick plan for FinBot PoC (notes)

Marissa / Ben - quick internal notes after reading Sophie’s workbook: 

- Action items before SE call:
  1) Review finbot-token-costs.xlsx and compute token-normalized baseline (I’ll add a tab for blended scenarios).
  2) Prepare microbenchmark: sample 1k requests with identical prompt distribution and measure cost/latency for:
     - baseline hosted model (replicate their provider where possible)
     - quantized 8-bit LLM variant (same architecture)
     - with and without KV/prefix cache + batching to show delta.
  3) Prepare short slide: integration effort summary for sidecar vs no-sidecar.

- Hypothesis: batching + KV cache should deliver ~30-50% cost improvement alone; quantization + optimized kernels can get us into the 2-3x range depending on quality trade-offs.

I’ll have the spreadsheet + microbenchmark plan ready by EOD Mon; can use that to drive the SE session.

-
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
